subject: Geo deployment eligibility & private networking questions (SOC 2 / CAIQ follow-up)
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@helioshealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@helioshealth.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: CAIQ follow-up: confirmation of regional hosting and private peering options

Hi Jasmine / Ben,

Thanks for turning around the CAIQ earlier this week — helpful. To close our internal risk review we have a few follow-ups specific to deployment geography and private network connectivity:

- Can Redwood confirm whether Helios workloads can be pinned to a single AWS region (us-east-1) and that data at rest for that customer will not be replicated to other regions without an explicit request? We need a short written commitment or pointer to the control that enforces region constraints.

- For private deployments: do you support a direct VPC peering / AWS PrivateLink / Transit Gateway (TGW) setup into a Redwood Private environment? If so, what level of control will Helios have over peering ACLs/route tables? We need an architecture-level answer + contact for networking engineers.

- Any SOC 2 control references that map specifically to data locality and egress controls (e.g., logs, backups, disaster recovery replicas)? A one-page list is perfect.

We appreciate the attachments you already sent in the CAIQ, but we need the above summarized for our procurement & InfoSec gate. If you can provide a short runbook or diagram and a named contact for the network engineer who would run a peering test, that will speed approvals.

Thanks,

Maria Gomez
Security Program Manager
Helios Health

Attachments referenced: N/A
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@helioshealth.com>, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@helioshealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CAIQ follow-up: confirmation of regional hosting and private peering options

Hi Maria / Alex,

Thanks — looping in Laura (Security) and Ben (Account) to provide concise answers and the artifacts you asked for. High-level answers below; Laura will follow with the SOC 2 / topology files and the sig spreadsheet.

- Region pinning: Yes — for customers on Redwood Private we offer region scoping. We can bind your deployment to a specified AWS region (us-east-1) and our private control plane will not replicate customer S3 objects or KV backups to other regions by default. We will provide the control reference (config flag + audit log event) and an exportable statement for procurement.

- Private connectivity: Redwood Private supports both Transit Gateway attachments (recommended for multi-VPC designs) and AWS PrivateLink endpoints. Peering is customer-controlled for route table and security policy — Redwood will provide the peering/endpoint configuration steps and a contact for the network run. The ops contact for a hands-on test is laura_bennett@redwood.com.

- SOC 2 references: Laura will enumerate the specific CC controls that map to data residency, egress monitoring, and backup retention. We'll attach a one-page SOC 2 summary plus a network topology diagram.

Action items here from Redwood:
1) Laura: attach SOC2 summary + network diagram + SIG/CAIQ cell answers.
2) Ben: share contract clause template for region-scoping (if Helios wants it in the MSA).

Ill leave the details to Laura and Ben — we should be able to give you a tidy packet by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Cell: (415) 555-0192

Attachments: none
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@helioshealth.com>, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@helioshealth.com>
Cc: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CAIQ follow-up: confirmation of regional hosting and private peering options

Hi Maria / Alex — attaching the items requested. Quick summary here so your reviewers don't have to dig:

1) redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (attached) — one-page mapping of SOC 2 CC controls to data residency, egress monitoring, and backup/replication controls. Key points:
   - Customer data can be scoped to a single region for Redwood Private. Config change events emit an audit record (audit.event:region_change) stored in our immutable audit log (90 days online, archived encrypted for 2 years per standard retention policy).
   - Backups for Private deployments are scoped per-customer and stored in-region by default; out-of-region replicas require an explicit change request that is gated by our security reviews.

2) network-topology-diagram.png (attached) — shows two supported architectures:
   - TGW attachment: recommended for customers with multiple VPCs. Redwood owns the private deployment VPC; Helios controls the side attachment and route table entries.
   - PrivateLink endpoint: supported for single-VPC integrations; endpoint interface in your VPC -> PrivateLink to Redwood service.

3) sig-response-20261208.xlsx (attached) — CAIQ / SIG rows we filled that are most relevant to your asks (networking, data locality, KMS partitioning).

Short answers to the three bullets in your first note:
- Region pinning: Supported and enforceable. We will supply a signed statement and MSA language if required.
- Peering options: TGW (recommended) or PrivateLink. Helios maintains control over route tables, SGs, and NACLs on your side; Redwood provides the required peer-side configuration and a test plan.
- SOC 2 mapping: See the attached summary; relevant control IDs called out in the document (CC6, CC7 equivalents).

Network runbook excerpt (included in the diagram PDF):
- Pre-req: Exchange VPC account IDs + operator CIDR ranges.
- Step 1: Redwood creates TGW attachment and proposes routes.
- Step 2: Helios adds route table entries for app subnets -> TGW.
- Step 3: Validation: packet captures and simple curl to /health endpoint over PrivateLink/TGW tunnel.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-min engineering call to run the test and walk through the diagram — Laura (me) and our infra engineer Mark OMalley (mark.omalley@redwood.com) can join.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (PDF, 142KB); network-topology-diagram.png (PNG, 438KB); sig-response-20261208.xlsx (XLSX, 54KB)

--
Laura Bennett
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@helioshealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@helioshealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CAIQ follow-up: confirmation of regional hosting and private peering options

Laura / Jasmine — this is perfect, thank you. A couple quick clarifying items before we close our procurement packet:

- For the audit log retention you noted 90 days online + 2 years archived. Can you confirm the archived logs are encrypted with a Helios-managed KMS key, or is it Redwood-managed? We need that detail for our control owners.

- On the explicit out-of-region replica flow: can you outline the approval path (who signs off internally at Redwood) and whether that change is tracked in the same immutable audit log you referenced?

If you can reply with one-line answers to the two items above, well be ready to approve and (pending the contract clause) aim for an onboarding window in January.

Cheers,
Alex
VP, IT Operations | Helios Health
